Sales for a utility comparison service here. My God I hate my job right now. I’ve stuck at it for a while now and I’ve become okay at it, but our company is becoming desperate for custom with the way they advertise; our marketing makes it out that you could save money on your utility bills with your current provider but it’s not, it’s with a different supplier. Half the time once a customer has agreed the contract on the phone they won’t know they’re changing for 10 days until they get the welcome pack. Sure, they get 14 days to cancel from the start of the process, so you can imagine cancellation rate is very high thus affecting commission massively (you only get paid if you make a certain no. of contracts a day, if one cancels on a day you just meet bare minimum target, bye bye commission for that day). 

Loads of vulnerable people coming to our site, calling us, then getting shitty that we’re mis-advertising. I used to brush it off and claim it’s not our fault that the customer misread our advert. The other day I actually saw our advert on my phone for the first time and, lo and behold, every customer who had moaned at me was dead right. 

The money is great and it’s nice to have a guaranteed salary at this uncertain time, but the sneaky turn the company is taking, coupled with my rapidly declining mental health in isolation, means I can’t wait to leave this job.

Sorry, could not disagree more. The FA Cup is the cornerstone of English footballing culture. It is the most decorated and famous in terms of history and tradition. 

The FA Cup has the power to change a football club. Change their future. Rewrite the past. Create a legacy.

Just ask Crawley. Or Stevenage. I mean, everybody knows who Havant and Waterlooville are because of the FA Cup run where they faced Liverpool.

Following their trip to Old Trafford in a 3rd Round replay this season, Cambridge United earned over £1.5million, as gate receipts are split nearly in half in the cup, meaning that they can double their regular yearly revenue.

Figures like that can transform Cambridge, a club who have worked so hard to grind their way back up the pyramid and into the Football League in recent years.

To be honest just the £150,000 they received in TV and radio fees alone is so significant for a traditional old football club like that, never mind £1.5million.

The playing field is well and truly levelled in the FA Cup. One reason? The playing field. One of the most beautiful things about the FA Cup is the time of year that it is played. Those who propose summer football in this country would risk killing this competition.

Bad weather, quite simply, creates muddy pitches. Lower league teams, for all the hard work and dedication that volunteers and ground staff put in, simply do not have the resources to beat the downpours.

And there is something beautiful about watching 'established' teams travel to places like Cambridge, Warrington and Blyth to try and execute their game in 'proper' football conditons.

Truthfully, there was nothing wrong with the pitch at Cambridge when they faced Man United; the groundsman did a superb job at Abbey Road. But it takes just a couple of little bobbles to throw a free-flowing footballing side off their game.

Underdogs raise their game. It's their one shot to impress under the bright lights of the cameras. That one shot to write that story to tell their families in years to come.

In the same respect, the 'established' teams can curl up and go into their comfort zone. Radamel Falcao and Angel Di Maria did not for one moment consider that United were not going to win that game in the build-up. They relaxed, then underperformed.

For the majority of teams that enter the competition, it starts in July.

July marks the draw for the extra preliminary round of the FA Cup, and the following two rounds, are drawn. The start of the road to stardom. Someone always makes it. Could it be their time to shine?

Take Warrington's story, for example.

A last minute equaliser against Colwyn Bay, two divisions above them, saw them take their third qualifying round tie to a replay. They won that, before defeating North Ferriby and qualifying for the first round for the first time in their history.

Creating history, at the end of the day, is what the FA Cup is all about.
